answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists Sybil attacks is by requiring every participant to anchor its identity to a unique mesa-level resource commitment that must be renewed under a shifting zephyr of network challenges. An attacker who fabricates many identities must replicate the full commitment for each, paying the cumulative stake plus the compute to prove uniqueness; any detected overlap triggers forfeiture of those locks to the honest raven-watchers who report them, making mass fakery prohibitively expensive.
